author: Thomas à Kempis
title: On the contemplation of human misery

verses.text: Thou art miserable wheresoever thou art, and whithersoever thou turnest, unless thou turn thee to God.
verses.modernizedText: You are miserable wherever you are and wherever you turn, unless you turn to God.

verses.text: Why art thou disquieted because it happeneth not to thee according to thy wishes and desires?
verses.modernizedText: Why are you troubled because things do not happen according to your wishes and desires?

verses.text: Who is he that hath everything according to his will?
verses.modernizedText: Who has everything according to his will?

verses.text: Neither I, nor thou, nor any man upon the earth.
verses.modernizedText: Neither I, nor you, nor anyone on earth.

verses.text: There is no man in the world free from trouble or anguish, though he were King or Pope.
verses.modernizedText: No one in the world is free from trouble or anguish, even if he is King or Pope.

verses.text: Who is he who hath the happiest lot?
verses.modernizedText: Who has the happiest lot?

verses.text: Even he who is strong to suffer somewhat for God.
verses.modernizedText: The person who is strong enough to suffer something for God.

verses.text: There are many foolish and unstable men who say, “See what a prosperous life that man hath, how rich and how great he is, how powerful, how exalted.”
verses.modernizedText: There are many foolish and unstable people who say, “See what a prosperous life that person has, how rich and great he is, how powerful, how exalted.”

verses.text: But lift up thine eyes to the good things of heaven, and thou shalt see that all these worldly things are nothing, they are utterly uncertain, yea, they are wearisome, because they are never possessed without care and fear.
verses.modernizedText: But lift up your eyes to the good things of heaven, and you will see that all these worldly things are nothing; they are utterly uncertain, indeed, they are wearisome, because they are never possessed without care and fear.

verses.text: The happiness of man lieth not in the abundance of temporal things but a moderate portion sufficeth him.
verses.modernizedText: Human happiness does not lie in an abundance of temporal things, but a moderate portion is enough.

verses.text: Our life upon the earth is verily wretchedness.
verses.modernizedText: Our life on earth is truly wretchedness.

verses.text: The more a man desireth to be spiritual, the more bitter doth the present life become to him; because he the better understandeth and seeth the defects of human corruption.
verses.modernizedText: The more a person desires to be spiritual, the more bitter the present life becomes to him, because he better understands and sees the defects of human corruption.

verses.text: For to eat, to drink, to watch, to sleep, to rest, to labour, and to be subject to the other necessities of nature, is truly a great wretchedness and affliction to a devout man, who would fain be released and free from all sin.
verses.modernizedText: For to eat, to drink, to watch, to sleep, to rest, to labor, and to be subject to the other necessities of nature is truly a great wretchedness and affliction to a devout person, who longs to be released and free from all sin.

verses.text: For the inner man is heavily burdened with the necessities of the body in this world.
verses.modernizedText: For the inner person is heavily burdened with the necessities of the body in this world.

verses.text: Wherefore the prophet devoutly prayeth to be freed from them, saying, Deliver me from my necessities, O Lord.(1) But woe to those who know not their own misery, and yet greater woe to those who love this miserable and corruptible life.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore the prophet devoutly prays to be freed from them, saying, Deliver me from my necessities, O Lord.(1) But woe to those who do not know their own misery, and greater woe still to those who love this miserable and corruptible life.

verses.text: For to such a degree do some cling to it (even though by labouring or begging they scarce procure what is necessary for subsistence) that if they might live here always, they would care nothing for the Kingdom of God.
verses.modernizedText: For some cling to it to such a degree, even though by laboring or begging they scarcely obtain what is necessary to live, that if they could live here always, they would care nothing for the Kingdom of God.

verses.text: Oh foolish and faithless of heart, who lie buried so deep in worldly things, that they relish nothing save the things of the flesh!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, foolish and faithless in heart, who lie buried so deep in worldly things that they relish nothing except the things of the flesh!

verses.text: Miserable ones! they will too sadly find out at the last, how vile and worthless was that which they loved.
verses.modernizedText: Miserable ones! They will discover all too sadly at the end how vile and worthless was what they loved.

verses.text: The saints of God and all loyal friends of Christ held as nothing the things which pleased the flesh, or those which flourished in this life, but their whole hope and affection aspired to the things which are above.
verses.modernizedText: The saints of God and all loyal friends of Christ counted as nothing the things that pleased the flesh or those that flourished in this life, but their whole hope and affection aspired to the things above.

verses.text: Their whole desire was borne upwards to everlasting and invisible things, lest they should be drawn downwards by the love of things visible.
verses.modernizedText: Their whole desire was carried upward to everlasting and invisible things, lest they be drawn downward by love of visible things.

verses.text: Lose not, brother, thy loyal desire of progress to things spiritual.
verses.modernizedText: Brother, do not lose your loyal desire to progress to spiritual things.

verses.text: There is yet time, the hour is not past.
verses.modernizedText: There is still time; the hour has not passed.

verses.text: Why wilt thou put off thy resolution?
verses.modernizedText: Why will you put off your resolution?

verses.text: Arise, begin this very moment, and say, “Now is the time to do: now is the time to fight, now is the proper time for amendment.”
verses.modernizedText: Rise, begin this very moment, and say, “Now is the time to act; now is the time to fight; now is the proper time for amendment.”

verses.text: When thou art ill at ease and troubled, then is the time when thou art nearest unto blessing.
verses.modernizedText: When you are ill at ease and troubled, then is the time when you are nearest to blessing.

verses.text: Thou must go through fire and water that God may bring thee into a wealthy place.
verses.modernizedText: You must go through fire and water so that God may bring you into a wealthy place.

verses.text: Unless thou put force upon thyself, thou wilt not conquer thy faults.
verses.modernizedText: Unless you put force upon yourself, you will not conquer your faults.

verses.text: So long as we carry about with us this frail body, we cannot be without sin, we cannot live without weariness and trouble.
verses.modernizedText: As long as we carry this frail body about with us, we cannot be without sin; we cannot live without weariness and trouble.

verses.text: Gladly would we have rest from all misery; but because through sin we have lost innocence, we have lost also the true happiness.
verses.modernizedText: We would gladly have rest from all misery, but because through sin we have lost innocence, we have also lost true happiness.

verses.text: Therefore must we be patient, and wait for the mercy of God, until this tyranny be overpast, and this mortality be swallowed up of life.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore we must be patient and wait for the mercy of God until this tyranny is past and this mortality is swallowed up by life.

verses.text: O how great is the frailty of man, which is ever prone to evil!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how great is human frailty, which is always prone to evil!

verses.text: To-day thou confessest thy sins, and to-morrow thou committest again the sins thou didst confess.
verses.modernizedText: Today you confess your sins, and tomorrow you commit again the sins you confessed.

verses.text: Now dost thou resolve to avoid a fault, and within an hour thou behavest thyself as if thou hadst never resolved at all.
verses.modernizedText: Now you resolve to avoid a fault, and within an hour you behave as if you had never resolved at all.

verses.text: Good cause have we therefore to humble ourselves, and never to think highly of ourselves, seeing that we are so frail and unstable.
verses.modernizedText: We have good cause, therefore, to humble ourselves and never think highly of ourselves, seeing that we are so frail and unstable.

verses.text: And quickly may that be lost by our negligence, which by much labour was hardly attained through grace.
verses.modernizedText: And what was hardly attained through grace by much labor can quickly be lost by our negligence.

verses.text: What shall become of us at the end, if at the beginning we are lukewarm and idle?
verses.modernizedText: What will become of us at the end if we are lukewarm and idle at the beginning?

verses.text: Woe unto us, if we choose to rest, as though it were a time of peace and security, while as yet no sign appeareth in our life of true holiness.
verses.modernizedText: Woe to us if we choose to rest as though it were a time of peace and security, while as yet no sign of true holiness appears in our life.

verses.text: Rather had we need that we might begin yet afresh, like good novices, to be instructed unto good living, if haply there might be hope of some future amendment and greater spiritual increase.
verses.modernizedText: Rather, we need to begin afresh like good novices, to be instructed in good living, so that perhaps there may be hope of some future amendment and greater spiritual growth.
